t: Minimum Inversion Count in Fixed-Length Windows — BIT Sliding Window
o: Slide a window of size k across nums, maintaining its inversion count incrementally: adding an element x on the right adds the number of current window elements greater than x; dropping the leftmost element y removes the number of remaining window elements smaller than y. A Fenwick tree over compressed values supports both counts in O(log n). Example: [3,1,2,5,4], k=3 → window [1,2,5] achieves 0.
k: Window inversions update locally: +count(>x) on insert, −count(<y) on evict.
Coordinate-compressed Fenwick trees give O(log n) rank queries; total O(n log n).

a.i: For each window, count inversions by pairwise comparison. Obvious and correct; O(nk) time.
s: For each start l, double-loop over the window counting pairs with a[i] > a[j].
a.t: O(n·k²) naive pairwise, or O(n·k log k) with per-window mergesort

a.i: Maintain the window's multiset in a BIT. Insertions and evictions adjust the running inversion count by rank queries, and we record the minimum once the window is full.
s: Compress values; build a BIT with add/point-prefix operations.
For each r: cur += count(> nums[r]); insert nums[r].
If r ≥ k: y = nums[r−k]; cur −= count(< y); delete y.
Once r ≥ k−1, update the answer minimum.
a.t: O(n log n) — two BIT operations per element
a.sp: O(n) for compression and the BIT

w: Present the BIT solution as the answer; the brute force only anchors correctness. Key subtlety: when evicting y, subtract count of strictly smaller elements still in the tree — earlier evictions guarantee these are exactly y's successors in the window. Watch duplicate handling (strict inequalities) and 64-bit inversion counts (up to ~5e9). Follow-up: report the argmin window, or handle streaming updates.
